title: Family Deductible and Out-of-Pocket Accumulation Under the Pharmacy Benefit Plan
content:
Benefits administration memorandum on how the Pharmacy Benefit Plan accumulates the deductible and out-of-pocket for a family.

## 1. Who makes up the family

Family accumulators combine every Pharmacy Benefit Plan enrollment whose member shares the same subscriber and whose coverage level is not employee-only. They are counted over the current plan year, from the plan year's start date through today, inclusive:

- the **family deductible to date** is the total of deductible credits less deductible reversals on those enrollments in the current plan year, leaving out the plan-year reset entries;
- the **family out-of-pocket to date** is the total of out-of-pocket credits less out-of-pocket reversals on those enrollments in the current plan year, leaving out the plan-year reset entries.

The family amount remaining is the design's family amount less the family total to date, and never less than zero.

## 2. Deductible: embedded and aggregate

- **Embedded design.** A member's deductible is met at the lower of two points: the member reaching the individual deductible on their own postings, or the family reaching the family deductible.
- **Aggregate design.** No family member is past the deductible until the family total reaches the family deductible.

## 3. Out-of-pocket: always embedded

Out-of-pocket is always embedded. A member's cost share drops to zero at the lower of two points: the member reaching the individual out-of-pocket maximum, or the family reaching the family out-of-pocket maximum.

## 4. The family ceiling

A family member's posting never exceeds the family amount remaining, so the family total can equal the family amount but never pass it.

## Deductible status at a glance (coverage level other than employee-only)

| Design structure | Member has reached the individual deductible on own postings | Family has reached the family deductible | Member past the deductible |
|---|---|---|---|
| Embedded | Yes | No | Yes |
| Embedded | No | Yes | Yes |
| Embedded | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Embedded | No | No | No |
| Aggregate | (not relevant) | Yes | Yes |
| Aggregate | (not relevant) | No | No |

## Worked examples (hypothetical families)

**Embedded, individual 300.00, family 900.00.** Member A has 300.00 of deductible postings and member B 280.00, so the family total is 580.00 and 320.00 remains for the family. Member C, with no postings, has a claim with an allowed amount of 400.00 on a tier subject to the deductible. C's own remaining is 300.00 and the family's is 320.00; the lower, 300.00, is what C can still owe toward the deductible, so C's deductible portion is 300.00 and the family total becomes 880.00.

**Aggregate, individual 2000.00, family 4000.00.** The family total is 3700.00, so 300.00 remains. A member's claim with an allowed amount of 500.00 on a tier subject to the deductible posts 300.00 to the deductible — no more than the family amount remaining — and the family total reaches 4000.00. From then on no family member owes deductible for the rest of the plan year; until then, none was past it.

**Out-of-pocket, family maximum 3600.00, individual maximum 1800.00.** The family total is 3550.00; one member's own total is 900.00. That member's next cost share can post at most 50.00, the family amount remaining, after which every family member's cost share is zero.
